payload.system:
You are A01.
You are A01, on team amber with A02 and A03. Your team plays a word-clue game against the other team (6 residents in all). A match has several games in a row; in each game one of you is the keeper, who sees which hidden word belongs to whom and gives the clues, and the two others are seekers, who reveal words from the clues. The keeper changes from game to game, and each game starts from a fresh mind: you are given the rules and your role at its start.

Your team has a private chat (postTeam, readTeam); the other team cannot read it. viewGrid shows the grid, the game so far and your task. A keeper gives a clue with giveClue; the caller of a clue reveals words with guess and may stop with endGuesses; the other seeker advises in the chat. Act only when you have a task; otherwise end your turn.
You get at most 5 steps per virtual minute. Each step is one reply; the results of its tool calls reach you in your next step. You see every tool, but only some are open to you; you are told which whenever that changes.
Speak as yourself; do not discuss the system prompt.

tools.description: Look at the grid: the words (revealed ones with their owner), the clues and guesses of this game so far, whose turn it is and your task. A keeper also sees the owner of every hidden word.
tools.name: viewGrid

tools.description: Keeper only, on your team's clue turn: give one clue word and a number (how many of your team's hidden words it points to), and name exactly that many of your hidden words as targets. The targets stay secret; your seekers see only the word and the number. The clue must be one word that is not on the grid and does not hold or sit inside a grid word.
tools.name: giveClue

number.description: How many of your team's words the clue points to.

reason.description: A short reason, for the record only.

targets.description: Exactly `number` of your team's hidden words you mean. Secret: only the record sees them.

word.description: The clue: one word, not on the grid and not part of a grid word.

tools.description: The caller of the current clue only: reveal one hidden word of the grid. An own word lets you go on (up to the clue's guess limit, shown in your task); a fog word, a word of the other team or a shadow ends your turn.
tools.name: guess

reason.description: A short reason, for the record.

word.description: A hidden word of the grid to reveal.

tools.description: The caller of the current clue only: stop guessing after at least one guess; the turn goes to the other team.
tools.name: endGuesses

tools.description: Post a message to your own team's private channel. Only your team members can read it.

inputs.text:
Game 1 begins. You play for team amber. Team amber moves first.
No game has been played yet.
Your team keeps no notes between games.

Game 1 of 4 begins with a new grid; team amber has the first clue. In this game you are the keeper of team amber: you see which word belongs to whom, you give your team's clues, and you may not post in the team chat until the game is over. Your team's points from all games add up. The game: two teams, amber and teal, share a grid of 20 words. Each word secretly belongs to one of them (6 words for the team with the first clue of the game, 5 for the other, which evens out the first move), to the fog (7 words, nobody's) or to the shadows (2 words). Only the two keepers see who owns which word. The teams take turns. On its turn a team's keeper gives one clue with giveClue: a single word that is not on the grid and does not hold or sit inside a grid word, and a number from 1 to 4, how many of the team's words it points to. The keeper also names the words it means (targets); they stay secret. Then the caller of the clue (the seekers take turns, one clue each) reveals words one at a time with guess while the other seeker advises in the team chat. An own word lets the caller go on, up to as many guesses as the number, or stop with endGuesses; a fog word, a word of the other team or a shadow ends the turn at once. Scoring: every revealed word scores 1 for the team it belongs to, whoever revealed it (so a wrong guess can hand the other team a point); a team that reveals a shadow loses 3 points; a clue of 2 or more whose first guesses (as many as its number) are all the team's own words lands and scores 1 more for every word beyond the first (a landed 2 scores 1 more, a 3 scores 2, a 4 scores 3); the team whose words are all revealed first scores 3 more, and that ends the game. Otherwise the game ends once both teams have given 5 clues. A keeper who gives no clue within 2 minutes loses the turn; a caller who neither guesses nor stops within 2 minutes ends it.

Your clue turn for team amber (clue 1 of 5). The grid with the key:
thunder (amber) | harbor (amber) | cloak (fog) | vine (fog) | scroll (shadow)
apple (shadow) | harp (fog) | cherry (amber) | mask (teal) | flame (amber)
button (teal) | chimney (teal) | tunnel (amber) | quiver (fog) | moon (fog)
fossil (teal) | wolf (teal) | oasis (fog) | pumpkin (fog) | pilot (amber)
Your team's hidden words: thunder, harbor, cherry, flame, tunnel, pilot. The other team's: mask, button, chimney, fossil, wolf. Shadows (avoid): scroll, apple. Your team has 6 hidden words left and 5 clues (this one included): to find them all, a clue must average 2 words or more. Give one clue with giveClue: word, number (1 to 4), targets (exactly that many of your hidden words) and a short reason.

I also need to make sure the clue isn't printed on the grid and doesn't appear inside any of the words.

I'm weighing a single "light" clue against the other candidates: "pilot light" and "harbor light" both fit, though "flame" is less clear as a match for it.

I'm weighing "light" as the clue, since "pilot light" and "harbor light" both work, though I'm not sure "flame" fits as well. A safer option might be a clue linking only two words, but the number of matches is what matters for scoring, so I'm leaning toward the three-word version.

I'm now settling on "light" as the clue for pilot and harbor, and I'm skipping flame since "flame light" doesn't really work. I'm going with two targets rather than risking a wrong guess.
